- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and prices are falling, model often over-anticipates recovery; reduce forecast by 1–4% for the next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 2-day lagged mean.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3–0.6) and prices show no clear trend, model overfits short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average for smoothing.  
- In early forecast windows (first 5–7 days), model often underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% bias toward higher prices if sentiment is rising.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is low and price is near historical low, model often fails to recognize support; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to avoid premature bottoming.
